1.title: Cost Management
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Cost Management. It covers the exam area Describe Azure management and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe factors that can affect costs in Azure. Explore the pricing calculator. Describe cost management capabilities in Azure. Describe the purpose of tags. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure management and governance (thirty to thirty-five percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Factors that affect costs
1.text: Factors that affect costs. Azure follows the consumption-based model (Module one), so the bill depends on what you deploy and use. for prices. Resource type. Each service has its own meters (V M hours, G B stored, operations); the size, tier and skew matter. Consumption. The more you use, the more you pay; stopping or deleting resources stops the charges (a stopped V M that is deallocated stops compute charges, but its disks still cost). Region (location). The same service can have different prices in different regions.

1.title: Factors that affect costs, continued
1.text: Factors that affect costs. Bandwidth. Inbound data is generally free; outbound data (to the internet or between regions) is charged. Subscription and account type. A free account, pay-as-you-go, an enterprise agreement and others have different rates and offers. Maintenance and operations. Management, monitoring and support plans add cost; software licenses add cost unless you bring your own. Azure Marketplace. Third-party products from the Marketplace have their own prices.

1.title: Factors that affect costs, continued
1.text: Factors that affect costs. The figure shows this: Factors that affect Azure costs.

1.title: Factors that affect costs, continued
1.text: Factors that affect costs. Ways to reduce cost. Reservations (reserved instances). Commit to one or three years of use for certain resources to get a lower price. Azure savings plan for compute. Commit to a fixed hourly spend for one or three years for a discount across compute services. Azure Hybrid Benefit. Use existing Windows Server or sequel Server licenses (with Software Assurance) on Azure to pay less.

1.title: Factors that affect costs, continued
1.text: Factors that affect costs. Spot virtual machines. Use unused capacity at a big discount, but Azure can evict the V M; good for interruptible work. Right-sizing and autoscaling. Use the smallest size that works and scale down when idle. Azure Advisor (Module fourteen). Gives cost recommendations such as removing idle resources. Exam tip: "Commit for one or three years to save" to reservation (or savings plan). "Use my existing Windows Server license" to Azure Hybrid Benefit. "Cheap but can be interrupted" to Spot V M. "Free in, charged out" to bandwidth.

1.title: The pricing calculator
1.text: The pricing calculator. The Azure pricing calculator is a free web tool that estimates the cost of Azure services before you deploy. Choose products, then set region, size, tier and quantity to see a monthly estimate. You can compare options and export or share the estimate. You can use it to plan before you buy; it does not need a deployed resource. It estimates new deployments. For existing resources, use Cost Management (below). A related tool, the Total Cost of Ownership (T C O) calculator, compares the cost of running workloads on-premises versus Azure over a period. Exam tip: Estimate a future deployment to pricing calculator. Compare on-premises to Azure to T C O (total cost of ownership) calculator. See what you are spending now to Cost Management.

1.title: Microsoft Cost Management
1.text: Microsoft Cost Management. Microsoft Cost Management (in the Azure portal) helps you monitor, allocate and optimize your Azure costs. Cost analysis. View and break down actual costs by resource, resource group, tag, service or time. Budgets. Set a spending limit for a scope and get alerts when it is near or reached. Alerts. Notifications for budgets, credit, and anomalies. Recommendations. Suggestions to cut cost, such as right-sizing (shown with Azure Advisor). Exports. Send cost data on a schedule to storage for reporting. Scopes. Analyze at management group, subscription or resource group level. A budget sends alerts but does not stop resources by default. Exam tip: "Set a spending limit and be notified" to budget with alerts. "See which resource group costs most" to cost analysis.

1.title: Tags
1.text: Tags. A tag is a name-value pair you attach to resources, resource groups or subscriptions to organize them. Example: Environment Production, Cost Center one thousand forty-two. Use tags to. Allocate and report costs by department, project or environment (cost analysis can group by tag). Organize and find resources and automate operations. Apply governance (such as owner and purpose). Key facts. Tags are not inherited by default: a tag on a resource group does not automatically apply to its resources. Azure Policy can require a tag or copy it from the group.

1.title: Tags, continued
1.text: Tags. You can have many tags per resource (a limit applies), and the same tag on many resources. Tags are metadata only: they do not change how a resource works. Exam tip: "Group costs by department" to tags. "Tags on the resource group apply to its resources automatically" to false (unless Azure Policy does it).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned deployment before creating anything. Which tool should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The Azure pricing calculator. The pricing calculator estimates costs for planned services without deployment.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. The finance team wants to see the costs of each department's resources in one report. What should be applied to the resources? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tags such as Department. Tags let cost analysis group and allocate cost by department.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company runs a steady workload for three years and wants a lower price in return for a commitment. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Reservations. A one- or three-year reservation gives a lower price for committed use.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which statement about tags is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tags are name-value pairs used to organize resources and track cost. Tags are metadata. They are not inherited by default and do not affect performance.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An organization wants to receive an alert when its monthly Azure spending reaches eighty percent of the planned amount. What should it create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A budget with alerts in Cost Management. Budgets in Cost Management send alerts at chosen thresholds.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company already owns Windows Server licenses and wants to reduce the cost of Windows V Ms on Azure. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Hybrid Benefit. Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you use existing eligible licenses on Azure.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which data transfer is generally free in Azure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Inbound data to Azure. Inbound is generally free; outbound and cross-region transfers are charged.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which factors affect Azure cost? Name three. Answer: Resource type, consumption, region, bandwidth, subscription type, Marketplace products. Question two. What does the pricing calculator do? Answer: Estimates the cost of planned Azure services before deployment. Question three. Which tool analyzes actual costs and sets budgets? Answer: Microsoft Cost Management.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a tag? Answer: A name-value pair attached to a resource, group or subscription for organization and cost tracking. Question five. Are tags inherited from the resource group by default? Answer: No. Question six. Which option uses spare capacity at a discount but can be evicted? Answer: Spot virtual machines.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Cost factors: resource type and size, consumption, region, bandwidth (out is charged, in is free), subscription type, Marketplace. Save money: reservations and savings plans (one or three years), Hybrid Benefit, Spot V Ms, right-size, Advisor. Pricing calculator: estimate a planned deployment before you create anything. Cost Management: analysis, budgets and alerts, recommendations, exports. Tags: name-value pairs for cost allocation and organization; not inherited by default. In the next module, we continue the course.
